properties.data:
the significantly in vivo-exposed compounds of GuHong for inhibition of drug-metabolizing enzymes and drug transporters
Induction of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4 by the test GuHong compounds hydroxysafflor yellow A, kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside, kaempferol-3-O-sophoroside, 8-hydroxycinnamic acid-8-O-glucoside, coumaric acid-4- O-glucoside, chlorogenic acid, and N-acetyl-L-glutamine was assessed using cryopreserved human hepatocytes from three donors (DJJ, NHI and YNS) in triplicate at concentrations of $1 \bar { , } ~ 5 \bar { , }$ and 50-fold of the unbound $\mathrm { C } _ { \mathrm { m a x } }$ of human subjects receiving intravenous GuHong at labeled dose, while for MGHC the test concentrations was $1 \mathfrak { s } , 5 \mathfrak { s } .$ , and 50-fold of total unbound $\mathrm { C } _ { \mathrm { m a x } } .$ Cell culture and induction studies were performed as previously described[9,26]. The negative control was a 0.08% DMSO solution. Positive inducers for CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4

text:
the significantly in vivo-exposed compounds of GuHong for inhibition of drug-metabolizing enzymes and drug transporters
Induction of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4 by the test GuHong compounds hydroxysafflor yellow A, kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside, kaempferol-3-O-sophoroside, 8-hydroxycinnamic acid-8-O-glucoside, coumaric acid-4- O-glucoside, chlorogenic acid, and N-acetyl-L-glutamine was assessed using cryopreserved human hepatocytes from three donors (DJJ, NHI and YNS) in triplicate at concentrations of $1 \bar { , } ~ 5 \bar { , }$ and 50-fold of the unbound $\mathrm { C } _ { \mathrm { m a x } }$ of human subjects receiving intravenous GuHong at labeled dose, while for MGHC the test concentrations was $1 \mathfrak { s } , 5 \mathfrak { s } .$ , and 50-fold of total unbound $\mathrm { C } _ { \mathrm { m a x } } .$ Cell culture and induction studies were performed as previously described[9,26]. The negative control was a 0.08% DMSO solution. Positive inducers for CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4 were omeprazole (50 μmol/L), phenobarbital (1 mmol/L), and rifampin (20 μmol/L), respectively. Fold induction was calculated using both enzyme activity and mRNA levels. The probe substrates for CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4 were phenacetin (100 μmol/L), bupropion (250 μmol/L), and midazolam (8 μmol/L), respectively. Differential enzyme activity between treated and untreated cells was defined as the treated/untreated cell ratio of enzyme activity (EA-T/U ratio) by measuring metabolite concentrations. A ratio of ≥2 for a test compound and a ratio of ≥20% of the positive control from at least one of the three donors indicated a positive induction. Cellular enzyme mRNA levels were determined by SYBR-based quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) analysis. The relative quantity of the target mRNA was determined using the ΔΔCt method. For the test compound, a ratio of enzyme mRNA levels between the treated and untreated cells (mRNA-T/U ratio) of ≥4 from at least one of the three donors indicated a positive result.The potential of GuHong to precipitate drug interactions was evaluated in vitro using significantly in vivo-exposed compounds, which were tested for their inhibition of drug-metabolizing enzymes and drug transporters listed in the International Council for Harmonization of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) M12 Guideline titled “Drug Interaction Studies” (https:// database.ich.org/sites/default/files/ICH\_M12\_Step4 Guideline\_2024\_0521\_0.pdf). The test in vivo-exposed GuHong compounds were hydroxysafflor yellow A, kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside, kaempferol-3-O-sophoroside, 8-hydroxycinnamic acid-8-O-glucoside, coumaric acid-4-O-glucoside, chlorogenic acid, N-acetyl-L-glutamine, and mixture of GuHong compounds (MGHC) (a mixture of the seven GuHong compounds).
